messages.author: 512610f4917ceaf3
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Julia C++ FFI interface
parts:
Clearly this is of great interest to Julia's Stan.jl package (and I'm following it quite closely). It is closer to Rcpp. 

Last week a new (v0.0.2) version of Stan.jl was tagged and pushed to METADATA, tested and available on Julia's 0.3_RC1 on OSX.

Version 0.0.2 version returns the sampling, diagnose and optimize results as an array of dictionaries (one dictionary for each chain), similar to a companion package Jags.jl (not yet published but available at https://github.com/goedman/Jags.jl.git ).

All 0.0.x releases do break compatibility as the Julia interface takes shape. Only after the 0.1.0 release I plan to start using the deprecate.jl abilities to alleviate the pain.

Version 0.0.3, in about 10 days, will generate input data from a dictionary and, if necessary, regenerate and compile model files based on a Stan model defined as a Julia string. Similar code is working in Jags.jl.

Version 0.0.4 will focus on plotting of the results, similar to Julia's (unpublished yet) Mamba.jl package using Gadfly.jl and Winston.jl.

It is the intention that some of FFI stuff will be part of the first 0.1.0 release later this year.

I also expect to take a closer look at Tim Holy's (and others) HDF5.jl package (more so if Stan would go there).

A final consideration is if 'bottling' CmdStan is a viable option (and/or a Homebrew formula?). Time frame tbd.

For both 'bottling' and FFI I want to make sure it is robust and kind of hidden from end-users.

Regards,
Rob J. Goedman
goe...@icloud.com
